claims.text: The high-temperature mechanical behavior of refractory HEAs is governed by heterogeneous lattice distortions.
The thermoelastic behavior of refractory HEAs is governed by heterogeneous lattice distortions.
Heterogeneous lattice distortions stabilize edge-dislocation cores through thermally activated super-jog formation.
The super-jog mechanism creates a high-temperature yield-strength plateau by balancing ordinary thermal softening.
The baseline NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 alloy was produced by cold rolling and annealing.
The baseline NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 alloy has high room-temperature tensile strength.
The baseline NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 alloy exhibits approximately temperature-independent strength between 673 K and 1073 K.
Replacing vanadium with an element of similar electronic character but closer atomic size would reduce overall lattice distortion.
A small compositional change of this type would change the heterogeneity of the lattice strain.
The degree of heterogeneous lattice strain affects dislocation-core structure, including the stabilization and activation of edge-dislocation super-jogs.
Local lattice distortions promote jog or super-jog formation on dislocations.
Super-jogs recover through thermally activated processes.
Super-jog-mediated resistance counterbalances elevated-temperature softening and produces a yield-strength plateau in highly distorted alloys.
The modified alloy with reduced lattice distortion will soften markedly as temperature increases, unlike the plateau-forming baseline.
The baseline NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 alloy has pronounced atomic-size mismatch and heterogeneous lattice strain.
The comparison is intended to hold the BCC phase, grain size, texture, processing route, atmosphere, and strain rate approximately constant.
Prior evidence qualitatively supports a connection between heterogeneous lattice strain, unusual jog or kink behavior, and strengthening.
The quantitative contribution and temperature dependence of super-jog formation remain uncertain.
